thread:
alex_support: FYI — enterprise customer hitting a 400 from /v1/embeddings after a client bump. Error: "Invalid embedding shape: expected (1536,) got (1,768)". They say it worked before.

oliver_eng: Can you paste the request body (sanitized)? Is this their JS client or python?

alex_support: JS. Customer sent a snippet:

alex_support: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1",
  "input": [["Welcome to our docs"], ["Get started"]]
}
```

rita_sre: Ahhh that double array looks suspicious — they wrapped each string in an array. Embeddings expects a string or an array of strings, not array-of-array. Server tries to interpret inner arrays as tokens which causes downstream shape mismatch.

oliver_eng: Exactly. When the tokenizer path gets an array instead of raw text it can produce a vector set with the wrong dims depending on the code path. Ask them to send:

oliver_eng: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1",
  "input": ["Welcome to our docs", "Get started"]
}
```

alex_support: I sent that back, plus a quick repro snippet they can run:

alex_support: ```js
// buggy: double-wrapped strings
await client.embeddings({ model: 'redwood-embed-large-v1', input: [["a"],["b"]] })

// fixed:
await client.embeddings({ model: 'redwood-embed-large-v1', input: ["a","b"] })
```

maria_docs: We should add a short note in the embeddings docs and FAQs with the common JSON shapes (single vs batch) and a sample bad payload. I'll add a small example and link it from errors.

oliver_eng: Also saw cases where people pass the vector floats to the embeddings endpoint (e.g., trying to upsert instead of request). That returns a very confusing shape error too. We should make the API error hint: "Are you passing raw vectors? Expected text or array of text."

rita_sre: There's also a throughput angle — customer moved to batching to save tokens but used super-large batches (1000 items) and hit latency spikes + 429s. Recommend batch size ~32-128 depending on model; for redwood-embed-large-v1 suggest 64 default.

alex_support: Customer said they saw a billing spike earlier today when they tried nested batching via their queue — we confirmed retries blew up. I recommended exponential backoff and capping concurrency.

oliver_eng: For follow-up: I can push a runtime validation that detects nested arrays of strings vs strings and return a clearer 422 with example payload. Low-risk change. Also add logging to capture example payload shapes for triage.

maria_docs: I'll draft the docs blurb. rita, can you add a note in the incident runbook about «embedding shape» so oncall can quickly grep common patterns?

rita_sre: Yep. Will add it. Also setting an alert on sudden uptick of 4xx from /v1/embeddings so we catch client regressions early. observability-bot: Created alert EMBD-4XX-spike (severity: low)

alex_support: Customer confirmed fix on their side (removed extra array) and errors went away. They also reduced batch size to 64 and latency improved. Closing for now but leaving doc/validation action items. :thumbsup:

oliver_eng: Nice. Quick PR to runtime + docs change will prevent churn.

maria_docs: I'll open a docs PR with examples and link to the alert.

alex_support: Thanks all!
